page7_img_1.png.title: Frequency of code-review comment categories from card sort
page7_img_1.png.description: A horizontal bar chart reporting how 570 CodeFlow review comments (200 threads) were categorized by a card sort. The largest slice is "Code Improvements" (165 comments, about 29%), followed by "Understanding" (≈125 comments, ~22%) and "Social Communication" (≈85 comments, ~15%). "Defects" appears fourth with 78 comments (~14%) and, as the paper notes, mostly concerns small logical/micro issues; "Knowledge Transfer" is very small (12 comments, ~2%). The distribution highlights that reviewers left many stylistic/clarifying comments and relatively fewer defect reports, supporting the paper’s claim that modern reviews produce more improvement and understanding-oriented feedback than deep defect-finding.

page4_img_1.png.title: Mixed‑method research workflow for studying modern code review (steps 1–6)
page4_img_1.png.description: A process diagram illustrating the study’s six-step mixed-method methodology, organized into Data Collection (left), Data Analysis (center), and Validation (right). The left side shows how a previous study and 17 in‑person observations/interviews (with an iterative interview‑guideline loop) produced transcripts, while CodeFlow review data produced review threads. The center depicts two parallel card‑sorts — one on 1,047 interview “logical units” and one on 570 review comments — whose results feed into an affinity diagram (step 5). The affinity diagram then informed two validation surveys: a managers’ survey (165 respondents) and a programmers’ survey (873 respondents), showing the triangulation and flow between qualitative coding and quantitative validation.

page8_img_1.png.title: Surveyed level of code-understanding needed for different review outcomes
page8_img_1.png.description: A horizontal stacked-bar chart titled “Level of Understanding Needed” shows survey responses for ten review outcomes (Finding Defects, Alternative Solutions, Share Code Ownership, Knowledge Transfer, Team Assessment, Code Improvement, Improve Dev Process, Team Awareness, Track Rationale, Avoid Build Breaks). Each bar is divided into four segments (None=white, Low=light gray, High=dark gray, Complete=black). Finding Defects and Alternative Solutions have the largest dark-gray plus black portions, indicating most respondents said these outcomes require high or complete understanding; mid-ranked items (e.g., Share Code Ownership, Knowledge Transfer, Team Assessment, Code Improvement) show a mix of low and high needs. Lower-ranked items such as Track Rationale and Avoid Build Breaks show larger white/light-gray segments, meaning many respondents felt less understanding was needed. This pattern supports the paper’s claim that deep change/context understanding is especially important when the goal is finding defects or proposing alternative solutions.

page3_img_1.png.title: CodeFlow review UI showing file list, reviewer status, diff view, inline discussion, and comment summary
page3_img_1.png.description: Screenshot of the CodeFlow code-review tool showing five annotated regions: (1) a left-hand file list including a description.txt and changed files for the submission; (2) a reviewer-status pane that lists the author and reviewers with status icons and action buttons (e.g., Complete Review/Recall); (3) the main diff view that highlights changed lines in a source file and a vertical overview gutter for navigating the change; (4) an inline threaded comment popup attached to a specific changed line that contains multiple reviewer-author replies and a resolved/Hide control; and (5) a lower pane summarizing all review comments and their status (Active/Resolved) for the selected file. The view illustrates how CodeFlow combines file selection, reviewer presence, diff highlighting, persistent inline discussion threads, and a centralized comment summary to support synchronous or asynchronous, tool-based modern code review.

page6_img_1.png.title: Developers' ranked motivations for code review
page6_img_1.png.description: Stacked horizontal bar chart (n=873 developers) showing how respondents ranked motivations as top (black), second (gray), or third (white) choices. The two longest bars are "Finding Defects" (383 top, 204 second, 96 third = 683 total) and "Code Improvement" (337 top, 208 second, 135 third = 680 total), indicating these are the most-cited motivations and are nearly tied in overall importance. "Alternative Solutions" is the third-most-selected motivation (147 top, 202 second, 152 third = 501 total), while "Knowledge Transfer" and "Team Awareness" appear next (about 330 responses each). Lower-ranked items (Improve Dev Process, Avoid Build Breaks, Share Code Ownership, Track Rationale, Team Assessment) receive substantially fewer top-three mentions, showing a long tail of secondary motivations.
